RIGHT only changed the HUD (row 0, column 2). So the arrow keys don't move the selected plus. The selection frame and the ring remain.
So: MOUSE click selects a plus (G frame), and a gray ring appears on tile (1,3). What is this ring? Maybe clicking a plus "places" something... hmm, wait. Maybe the ring is a "hole" or "crack" that appears on a random/adjacent tile as a penalty? Or maybe the ring indicates a "target" where the selected plus should be moved, and the movement is done by clicking the target?
Let me try clicking the ring tile (19, 30) — the center of the ring. If the game is "select a plus, then click a destination to move it," then clicking the ring tile should move the plus there.
Or maybe the game is like this: the plus is a "seed," and clicking it plants it, and the ring is a "sprout"...
Let me think about known games with this kind of mechanic: "L-shaped board, plus-shaped tiles, click to select, a ring appears on a different tile." This might be a "matching" game: click two tiles? When I clicked the plus at (1,1), a ring appeared at (1,3)... maybe the ring marks the "pair" of the clicked plus? But (1,3) is an empty tile.
Hmm, wait, maybe I misread the ring's position. The ring is at columns 29–32, rows 18–21. The plus at (1,4) is at columns 35–38, rows 18–21. The tile at columns 29–32 is the tile between the plus at (1,2) (columns 23–26) and the plus at (1,4) (columns 35–38). So the ring is on an empty tile.
Maybe the game is a "light up / paint" game: click a plus to select it, and the ring shows... hmm.
Or: the ring is where the plus "will fall"? Like a gravity game?
Let me try clicking the ring tile and see what happens. If the plus moves to the ring, then the mechanic is: click a plus → a ring appears at some destination → click the ring to move. But why does the ring appear at (1,3) and not somewhere else? Maybe the ring always appears at a fixed "target" position, and the goal is to move all the plus tiles to their respective target rings. When you click a plus, its target ring is displayed.
Actually, that makes sense as a puzzle: each plus has a target (ring). Click the plus to select it, then click the target to move it? Or after selecting, click the target tile to move the plus there.
Let me test: click the ring at (19,30).
